newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Commerzbank sees profit rise, may up payout.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Commerzbank sees profit rise, may up payout.

text.p: Commerzbank AG on Friday held out the prospect of its first dividend increase since 1994, provided earnings in 1997 meet the group's high expectations.

Chief executive Martin Kohlhaussen told shareholders a double-digit percentage rise in operating earnings was possible in 1997 after the group reported first-quarter operating profit before loan loss provisions rose 20.5 percent.

"Overall the good figures for the first quarter of the year and the further development in April justify our confidence that the Commerzbank Group will be able to increase its operating profit again in 1997," Kohlhaussen said.

"I believe we can be confident that, given continued good business during the course of the year, the management board will be able to propose room for manoeuvre for the dividend to the supervisory board."
Commerzbank's shares ended floor trade down one mark at 50.20 marks and rose slightly to 50.36 marks in late electronic dealings.

Kohlhaussen reiterated that Commerzbank did not view itself as a takeover target, rejecting persistent market speculation in recent months that it may fall prey to a foreign predator as part of expected consolidation in the German banking sector.

"We get so many calls asking us if we're about to be taken over that we have stopped issuing denials and now just decline comment," Kohlhaussen said. "But I can tell you there is nothing in the rumours."
Commerzbank would remain among the successful European banking groups at the turn of the millennium, he said.

Kohlhaussen noted that the bank's market value had more than trebled in the last four years to 20 billion marks and that Commerzbank's share price had jumped by more than 50 percent in the last year to more than 50 marks.
The bank had no concrete plans for a capital increase but was asking shareholders for approval to create authorised capital to give itself room for manoeuvre, Kohlhaussen said.
It aims to increase its core capital ratio to six percent by the year 2000 from 5.2 percent through accumulating retained earnings rather than tapping capital markets, Kohlhaussen said.

Referring to Commerzbank's investment banking plans, Kohlhaussen said the bank will expand its equity business more strongly and may hire new staff following the appointment of Memet Dalmat as head of its global equities business.
Kohlhaussen reiterated the bank's aim to expand its investment bank business through organic growth rather than acquisitions.
On the domestic retail side, the bank plans to merge 20 small branches in Germany this year to boost efficiency in the network. Kohlhaussen said the move need not lead to job losses.
The bank in 1996 reduced the number of its branches by 15 to 1,045.
